method_selection.citation: gauge-fixing rationale (per-user constant shifts leave the metric invariant); pairwise-consistency literature.
method_selection.why: The parent learning-curve fields are missing, so overfit or underfit is not supported. The clearer issue is objective/evaluator mismatch: GAUC and nDCG depend on within-user ordering, while ordinary BCE can spend capacity learning irrelevant per-user logit offsets. User-centered BCE removes that gauge freedom while retaining the accepted stack's BPR term. It is cheap, compatible with complete user-group batches, and has a measured +0.0026 gain—large enough to plausibly clear the run's 0.002 convergence threshold.

rejected.reason: It targets the same mismatch but is unmeasured, more complex, and likely offers only a small gain over the grouped BPR already present in the accepted package.
Temporal splitting makes shift plausible, but prior recency weighting failed on this dataset and this learned replacement has only an estimated ±0.0005 effect, below the convergence threshold.
Potentially useful for duration-related metric mismatch, but it is running elsewhere and has higher implementation risk than the measured-win gauge-fixed objective.

expected_delta_basis: The gauge-fixed-bce method card reports a measured +0.0026 over a 0.6018-family parent in run_novel_r1 node_003 by removing per-user logit shifts that GAUC and nDCG ignore.

hypothesis: Because the parent provides no usable learning-curve telemetry and fixed recency weighting was flat, learning late-period probabilities with an adversarial temporal classifier and using them as importance weights will address the defensible train-time data shift and improve validation primary by approximately 0.0005 over uniform weighting.
change_summary: Because the parent provides no usable learning-curve telemetry and fixed recency weighting was flat, learning late-period probabilities with an adversarial temporal classifier and using them as importance weights will address the defensible train-time data shift and improve validation primary by approximately 0.0005 over uniform weighting.

method_selection.citation: adversarial validation practice (e.g. Lightweight Boosting with Adversarial Validation, 2023).
method_selection.why: Learning-curve telemetry is missing, so overfit or underfit is unsupported. The known temporal train/validation boundary makes data shift the defensible diagnosis. Fixed recency weighting already failed on this dataset, while this untried atomic method learns the shift shape from train-period days rather than assuming an exponential half-life. Expected gain is honestly small and uncertain (about +/-0.0005), but 13 iterations remain, so screening this novel mechanism now is preferable to prematurely closing with another ensemble.

rejected.reason: Already tried on this dataset and rejected; repeating fixed exponential weighting would violate the instruction to avoid failed openings.
Uses another hand-specified recency schedule and has a lower expected gain of only +0.0001..+0.0007.
Its temporally local negative-sampling effect is speculative and similarly sub-noise; learned importance weights more directly test whether the temporal distributions differ.

expected_delta_basis: The adversarial-validation card predicts a small uncertain gain from learning the shift shape, while journal node_003 found that the fixed seven-day recency assumption did not produce a meaningful improvement.
